rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here miskīn means a weak, helpless person, including someone disabled in body; this usage concerns capacity rather than ownership or wealth.
rows.anchor: لضعفاء لا يقدرون على مدافعة الظلمة جمع مسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If miskīn means needy, the verse supports jurists who say a miskīn may own some property yet lack enough; that is not the word's meaning here.
rows.anchor: وقد يفسر بالمحتاج وحينئذ تكون الآية ظاهرة فيما يدعيه القائل المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those defining miskīn as owning nothing say the boat was not theirs but hired or borrowed; the author says this opposes the apparent wording without evidence.
rows.anchor: أن السفينة لم تكن ملكا لهم بل كانوا أجراء فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view compassionately describes the crew as people with nothing; Ali's reading intensifies the plural, possibly meaning sailors, boat steers, or hide tanners, with sailors judged most apparent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه ( لمساكين ) بتشديد السين جمع تصحيح لمساك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crew earned their livelihood through the boat; collective attribution of work fits a mixed crew including disabled men or the principle that agents' work counts for their principals.
rows.anchor: يعملون بها فيه ويتعيشون بما يحصل لهم وإسناد العمل إلى الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr intended to make the boat defective, not drown its occupants; the wording clarifies purpose and rejects reading the damage as an unintended consequence.
rows.anchor: أي أجعلها ذات عيب بالخرق ولم أرد إغراق من بها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير، قتادة، أبو عبيد، ابن السكيت، الزجاج
rows.claim: They read warāʾahum as before them; the author says Arabic usage permits this, though linguists dispute other contexts and many regard the word as genuinely opposite in direction.
rows.anchor: وبذلك قرأ ابن عباس وابن جبير وهو قول قتادة وأبي عبيد وابن السكيت والزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labīd, Sawwār al-Muḍarrib, and another poet use warāʾ for what is ahead, supporting the before-them interpretation.
rows.anchor: أليس ورائي إن تراخت منيتي لزوم العصا تحنى عليها الأصابع

rows.speaker: ابن الكمال، الزمخشري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Kamāl, quoting al-Zamakhsharī, defines warāʾ as the direction hidden from a person, whether behind or in front.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن الكمال نقلا عن الزمخشري : إنها اسم للجهة التي يواريها الشخص

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī explains warāʾ by grammatical relation; the author objects that 57:13 uses it for behind despite the word's relation to the object.
rows.anchor: ورد عليه بقوله تعالى ( ارجعوا وراءكم ) فإن وراء أضيفت فيه إلى المفعول

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ denies using warāʾ for a person physically before someone, allowing that sense only for times, nights, and days.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : لا يجوز أن يقال للرجل بين يديك هو وراءك

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains before as an extended use: opposite directions can each be behind the other when facing is irrelevant, as with two stones.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي : إنما جاز استعمال وراء بمعنى أمام على الاتساع لأنها جهة مقابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A common reading takes the king as behind the crew; the objection that they had escaped is answered by saying he was pursuing them or they would return into his reach.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأنه إذا كان خلفهم فقد سلموا منه وأجيب بأن المراد أنه خلفهم مدرك لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports variously name the king Hudad b. Baddad, Jalandi b. Karkar of Ghassān, or Mufawwad b. al-Jalandi in al-Andalus.
rows.anchor: واسمه على ما يزعمون هدد بن بدد وكان كافرا وقيل : جلندي بن كر كر

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy reads every boat as sound or usable, explaining why Khidr damaged this boat: the king seized sound boats.
rows.anchor: أي صالحة وقد قرأ كذلك أبي بن كعب ولو أبقى العموم على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghصببان is an accusative verbal noun specifying the kind of seizure; apparently the king took boats and did not return them, though another view says he requisitioned and returned them.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه كان يغصب السفن من أصحابها ثم لا يردها عليهم وقيل كان يسخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal sequence explains that Khidr protected a helpless crew from the king's habitual seizure; poverty is the stronger reason, while the king's practice clarifies the motive.
rows.anchor: أما السفينة فكانت لقوم مساكين عجزة يكتسبون بها فأردت بما فعلت إعانتهم

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ reports Khidr told the owners he sought their good after the boat escaped, they praised his judgment, and he repaired it; the author doubts this because Moses was apparently present.
rows.anchor: إنما أردت الذي هو خير لكم فحمدوا رأيه وأصلحها لهم كما كانت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boy's parents means his father and mother, with masculine plural formed by grammatical predominance; their names are reported as Azīr and Sahwāʾ.
rows.anchor: أي أبوه وأمه ففيه تغليب واسم الأب على ما في الإتقان

rows.speaker: أبي، ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ubayy's codex and Ibn ʿAbbās's reading explicitly call the boy an unbeliever; some infer he was adult, since a child is not literally described as believing or disbelieving.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي وقراءة ابن عباس ( وأما الغلام فكان كافرا وكان أبواه )

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawī answers that this reading is anomalous and not proof, or that the boy was named for what he would become had he lived.
rows.anchor: أن القراءة شاذة لا حجة فيها الثاني أنه سماه بما يؤل إليه لو عاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim says the boy was stamped an unbeliever at birth; the author remains cautious about related reports and says they do not undermine the sound view that children are in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم أن الغلام طبع يوم طبع كافرا

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري، الجحدري
rows.claim: They read the parents as nominative dual muʾminān; grammarians explain this through an implicit pronoun of circumstance, a dialect form, or the boy as subject of kāna.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو سعيد الخدري والجحدري ( فكان أبواه مؤمنان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khashiya means intense fear that the boy, if he lived, would engulf his believing parents in transgression against divine limits and unbelief.
rows.anchor: فخفنا خوفا شديدا أن يغشى الوالدين المؤمنين لو بقي حيا

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says parental love might lead them to follow the boy into unbelief; tyranny before unbelief intensifies the warning or depicts faith first stained and then removed.
rows.anchor: بأن يحملهما حبه على متابعته كما روى عن ابن جبير

rows.speaker: بعض شراح البخاري
rows.claim: Some commentators on al-Bukhārī take khashiya as knowledge: the boy would grow up inviting his parents to unbelief, and their love would make them comply.
rows.anchor: وفسر بعض شراح البخاري الخشية بالعلم فقال : أي علمنا أنه لو أدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the boy would overwhelm his parents through disobedience and ingratitude for their care, bringing them harm and distress.
rows.anchor: أن يغشيهما طغيانا عليهما وكفرا لنعمتهما عليه من تربيتهما إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view takes the phrase to mean that the boy's tyranny and unbelief would coexist with his parents' faith under one roof.
rows.anchor: ويقرن بإيمانهما طغيانه وكفره فيجتمع في بيت واحد مؤمنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say the boy committed wrongdoing or highway robbery and his parents protected him; adults are inferred, but the author favors those who say such conduct is implausible for a child.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أن الغلام كان يفسد وفي رواية يقطع الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers that Khidr himself answered Moses; al-Zamakhsharī allows that the words narrate God's statement, with khashiya figuratively meaning dislike, but this is less apparent.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا من كلام الخضر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says fear, hope, and similar expressions in God's speech address human listeners, since God is exalted above such states.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : إن الخوف والخشية كالترجي بلعل ونحوها الواقع في كلامه تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الأكثر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses zakāh as religion; most interpreters say it means purity from sins and bad traits.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : أي دينا وهو تفسير باللازم والكثير قالوا : أي طهارة من الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord-title signals God's intention to benefit the parents; raḥmā means mercy, as Ruʾba's poetic usage shows, and the phrase means more mercy and kindness toward them.
rows.anchor: وأقرب رحما 18 ( أي رحمة قال رؤبة بن العجاج : يا منزل الرحم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان، عطية
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers that the replacement child would be more merciful and dutiful; a report from ʿAṭiyya instead says the parents would be more compassionate toward the replacement.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن عطية أن المعنى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الثعلبي، يوسف بن عمر، جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Reports say the replacement was a girl who bore one or more prophets; al-Thaʿlabī says she married a prophet and bore a prophet who guided a nation, while Ibn ʿAṭiyya's objection is challenged.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس أنهما أبدلا جارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakāh and raḥmā are accusative specification nouns governed by the preceding comparative; the wording leaves the quality open, then explains it, and zakāh praises more than azkā.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب المصدرين على التمييز والعامل ما قبل كل من أفعل التفضيل

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān denies comparison because the boy had no purity or mercy; the author replies that he was pure in outward appearance whether a child or adult, and even an assumed shared quality permits comparison.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو حيان أن أفعل ليس للتفضيل هنا لأنه لا زكاة في ذلك الغلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the boy had no mercy is unsupported; on the parents-focused reading, mercy is central to the stated fear.
rows.anchor: وأن قوله : ولا رحمة قول بلا دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal fāʾ links the parents' fear to the wish for a replacement; the killing itself is not separately linked because its reason is delicately understood here, also rebutting Moses' implication of injustice.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الفاء للتفريع فيفيد سببية الخشية للإرادة المذكورة

rows.speaker: نافع، أبو عمرو، أبو جعفر، شيبة، حميد، الأعمش، ابن جرير
rows.claim: These authorities read yubaddilahumā with a doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر وشيبة وحميد والأعمش وابن جرير ( يبدلهما ) بالتشديد

rows.speaker: ابن عامر، أبو جعفر، يعقوب، أبو حاتم، ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and others read raḥmā with ḍamma on ḥāʾ; Ibn ʿAbbās reads it with fatḥa on rāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( رحما ) بفتح الراء وكسر الحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two orphan boys were probably young, since human orphanhood ends at puberty; Ibn ʿAṭiyya's suggestion that they were adults described as orphans compassionately is very unlikely.
rows.anchor: لأن يتم بني آدم بموت الأب وفي الحديث لا يتم بعد بلوغ

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows that the boys were adults, with orphan used compassionately for their former state; the author considers this remote.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : يحتمل أنهما كانا بالغين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is the earlier town; calling it a city here foregrounds the orphans and their righteous local father, unlike the earlier narrative's focus.
rows.anchor: هي القرية المذكورة فيما سبق ولعل التعبير عنها بالمدينة هنا

rows.speaker: عكرمة، قتادة
rows.claim: They identify the buried treasure as gold and silver; the author cites a report from Abū al-Dardāʾ transmitted by al-Bukhārī, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it.
rows.anchor: مال مدفون من ذهب وفضة كما أخرجه البخاري في تاريخه والترمذي

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines kanz as gathering wealth together and preserving it, from the expression for packing dates into a container.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الكنز جعل المال بعضه على بعض وحفظه وأصله من كنزت التمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the treasure belonged to the boys, it was likely inherited from their righteous father; blameworthy treasure is wealth from which due rights are withheld, not every stored asset.
rows.anchor: بأن الظاهر أن الكانز له أبوهما لاقتضاء ( لهما ) له إذا

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء، قتادة
rows.claim: A report says treasure was permitted to earlier communities while spoils were forbidden, and the reverse applies to this community; laws can differ by community.
rows.anchor: أحلت لهم الكنوز وحرمت عليهم الغنائم وأحلت لنا الغنائم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the treasure was not gold or silver but written leaves of knowledge; the same interpretation is related from Ibn Jubayr.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال : ما كان ذهبا ولا فضة ولكن كان صحف علم

rows.speaker: علي، أبو ذر، ابن عباس
rows.claim: A raised report from ʿAlī, a report from Abū Dharr, and a Companion-stopped report from Ibn ʿAbbās describe a gold tablet with maxims on providence, provision, death, judgment, and worldly instability.
rows.anchor: من حديث علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه مرفوعا والبزار عن أبي ذر كذلك

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's version, one side of the tablet bears the basmala and maxims; the other says God alone created good and evil, blessing those led to good and woe for those led to evil.
rows.anchor: أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا وحدي لا شريك لي خلقت الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some combine the treasure reports as types of buried wealth, but the author says this is strained and conflicts with Ibn ʿAbbās's explicit denial that it was gold or silver.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه على بعده يأباه ظاهر قول ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما ما كان ذهبا ولا فضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father may be the immediate father, reportedly named Kāshiḥ, or a more distant ancestor; reports place him as the tenth or seventh forefather, the latter attributed to Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن اسمه كاشح وأن اسم أمهما دهنا وقيل : كان الأب العاشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that a parent's righteousness brings divine care to descendants; reports from Jesus, Wahb, al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī, and Khaythama illustrate this protection and the father's trustworthiness.
rows.anchor: في الآية دلالة على أن صلاح الآباء يفيد العناية بالأبناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabbuka means your master and manager; addressing Moses with your Lord rather than their Lord urges submission and warns against disputing God's care of the boys.
rows.anchor: مالكك ومدبر أمورك ففي إضافة الرب إلى ضمير موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd is glossed as puberty, mature judgment, or strength; lexicographers give ages eighteen to thirty, while its plural-like form has disputed singular morphology.
rows.anchor: قيل أي الحلم وكمال الرأي وفي الصحاح القوة وهو ما بين ثماني عشر إلى ثلاثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr raised the wall to keep the treasure hidden until the boys could protect and use it; it was near collapse, the boys did not know of it, and their informed guardian was absent.
rows.anchor: ولولا أني أقمته لانقض وخرج الكنز من تحته قبل اقتدارهما على حفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raḥmatan is a purpose clause for God's willing the wall raised; the explicit phrase from your Lord replaces a pronoun, and it cannot be the purpose of the boys' extraction because the agents differ.
rows.anchor: مفعول له لأراد وأقيم الظاهر مقام الضمير وليس مفعولا له ليستخرجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection asks why from your Lord is repeated if the phrase already means God showed mercy or gives the purpose; an omitted clause, dropped preposition, or mercy meaning revelation are proposed alternatives.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأنه إذا كان أراد ربك بمعنى رحم كانت الرحمة من الرب لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the omitted-clause reading, Khidr says he acted hoping for God's mercy; and I did it not on my own authority confirms this.
rows.anchor: فيكون قوله ( وما فعلته عن أمري ( أي عن رأيي واجتهادي تأكيدا لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points either to the chain of outcomes just explained, with taʾwīl as eventual result, or to the explanation itself in its familiar sense.
rows.anchor: ( ذلك ( إشارة إلى ما ذكر من العواقب المنظومة في سلك البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tastaṭiʿ is the full form behind tasṭiʿ; the author explains its contraction by dropping the extra tāʾ for ease, while other etymologies are unnecessary.
rows.anchor: أي تستطع وهو مضارع اسطاع بهمز الوصل وأصله استطاع

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt lists four forms, including variants with altered or deleted tāʾ; the author finds the final deletion apt at the moment Moses and Khidr part.
rows.anchor: فاللغات أربع كما قال ابن السكيت : ما ألطف حذف أحد المتقارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the shortened form was saved for the final occurrence because it recurs in the story; others say it reflects Moses' relief at the explanation, but both explanations are challenged.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : إنما خص هذا بالتخفيف لأنه لما تكرر في القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl here may mean the outcome of what Moses saw or the explanation itself; the closing clause recaps earlier events and renews the rebuke.
rows.anchor: أي ذلك مآل وعاقبة الذي لم تستطع ( عليه صبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account assigns the first intention to Khidr's direct action, the second to God and Khidr because killing was Khidr's act but replacement God's, and the third to God alone.
rows.anchor: أنه الفاعل المباشر للتعييب وثانيا إلى ضمير المتكلم ومعه غيره

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī says the Prophet criticized Thābit b. Qays for joining God and His Messenger with a dual pronoun, treating the phrasing as improper equalization.
rows.anchor: وصرح الخطابي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كره منه ما فيه من التسوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other scholars allow shared pronouns for God and creatures in some contexts; views range from no objection to mild or severe dislike, depending on context and whether the speaker is the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وثانيها ما ذهب إليه الخطابي أنها تكره تنزيها وثالثها ما يفهمه كلام الغزالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author concludes shared pronouns are not objectionable in God's or the Prophet's speech; for ordinary people he favors context-sensitive, mild disapproval.
rows.anchor: أن الحق أنه لا كراهة في ذلك في كلام الله تعالى ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects taking we as jointly referring to God and Khidr, since it appears like we in we feared, which he does not take as shared; the rationale for we intended does not fit feared.
rows.anchor: لا أقول باشتراك هذا الضمير بين الله تعالى والخضر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposal says the first act was evil and assigned to Khidr, the third good and assigned to God, and the mixed second act to both; the author notes the same issue applies to we feared.
rows.anchor: الأسلوب : أن الأول شر فلا يليق إسناده إليه سبحانه وأن كان هو الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the pronoun shifts portray stages of realization, from self-agency to shared agency to recognizing God alone; the author rejects this as implausible or falsely attributing speech to Khidr.
rows.anchor: وقيل : اختلاف الأسلوب لاختلاف حال العارف بالله سبحانه فإنه في ابتداء أمره يرى نفسه مؤثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that God narrated different wording from what Khidr said, since God would not attribute to someone speech he never said or meant.
rows.anchor: فالله تعالى أجل وأعظم من أن ينقل عن أحد كلاما لم يقله أو لم يقل ما بمعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' first objection was less severe than the second; the experts hold nakran stronger than amran, so Khidr appropriately answered the first with a singular intention.
rows.anchor: بناء على ما اختاره المحققون من أن ( نكرا ) أبلغ من ( أمرا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains pronoun choice by Moses' changing objections: mild ship complaint gets I damaged it, the grave killing objection gets we feared and intended, and the mild wage complaint gets your Lord intended.
rows.anchor: والذي يخطر ببال العبد الفقير أنه روعي في الجواب حال الاعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If we includes Moses, the plural signals that the feared and intended threat was so grave that Moses would share in it, rather than independently condemn its basis.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك الإسناد إشارة إلى أن ما يخشى وما يراد قد بلغ في العظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: And I did it not on my own authority is clear evidence Khidr was a prophet; the theory that another prophet instructed him is unlikely and makes his special knowledge pointless.
rows.anchor: واستدل بقوله ( وما فعلته عن أمري ) القائلون بنبوته عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Khidr acted by inspiration, which would make inspiration binding law in his community; it cannot establish law in Moses' or our community, and even its proponents restrict it when scripture conflicts.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : كان ذلك عن إلهام ويلزمه القول بأن الإلهام كان حجة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked by Najda al-Ḥarūrī about killing children, Ibn ʿAbbās replied that only if one knew a child to be an unbeliever like Khidr could one kill; al-Subkī says this was a hypothetical to end the argument, not permission.
rows.anchor: كتب نجدة الحروري إلى ابن عباس يسأله عن قتل الصبيان

rows.speaker: اليافعي
rows.claim: Al-Yāfiʿī compares Khidr's certainty to a saint's inspiration permitting silk; the author calls this a grave error because inspiration is not binding law and prophetic law still governs.
rows.anchor: فما قاله اليافعي في روضه من أنه لو أذن الله تعالى لبعض عباده

rows.speaker: الشعراني
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī warns that many have gone astray by requiring action on inspiration and wrote a treatise opposing that doctrine.
rows.anchor: وممن صرح بأن الإلهام ليس بحجة من الصوفية الإمام الشعراني وقال : قد زل في هذا الباب

rows.speaker: ابن عربي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArabī says angelic inspiration is not revelation or a new divine command; after prophecy and law are complete, inspiration cannot create independent religious obligations.
rows.anchor: فإن الملك لا ينزل بوحي على غير قلب نبي أصلا ولا يأمر بأمر إلهي

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: Sirhindī says inspiration does not make the forbidden lawful or the lawful forbidden, so spiritual reality does not conflict with revealed law.
rows.anchor: بأن الإلهام لا يحل حراما ولا يحرم حلالا

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: Sirhindī rejects the idea that the true goal lies beyond religious law, calling that belief heretical and insisting that every rejected spiritual claim is false.
rows.anchor: أن المقصود الأصلي وراء الشريعة حاشا وكلا ثم حاشا وكلا

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: He says the spiritual path and religious law are the same in reality, with no contradiction even by a hair's breadth; anything that conflicts with law is rejected.
rows.anchor: فكل من الطريقة والشريعة عين الآخر لا مخالفة بينهما بقدر رأس الشعيرة

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: He says the inward path perfects outward law; apparent contradictions during an ecstatic state disappear when the seeker returns to sobriety.
rows.anchor: فإذا تجاوزوا ذلك المقام ورجعوا إلى الصحو ارتفعت تلك المنافاة بالكلية

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: Sirhindī says religious law has knowledge, action, and sincerity; Sufi practices serve to complete sincerity, and the law gathers all forms of happiness.
rows.anchor: للشريعة ثلاثة أجزاء علم وعمل وإخلاص فما لم تتحقق هذه الأجزاء

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: The route to nearness, whether prophetic or saintly, is only the law taught by the Messenger; other paths are deviation, as cited Qur'anic verses and reports affirm.
rows.anchor: فتقرر أن طريق الوصول إلى درجات القرب الإلهي جل شأنه سواء كان قرب النبوة

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: Sirhindī says Sufi knowledge at the end is the knowledge of religious law, though it becomes unveiled and immediate for them rather than theoretical and inferential.
rows.anchor: ففي نهاية النهايات علومهم علوم العلماء وهي علوم الشريعة

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: Experiences and spiritual insights may appear along the path, but the seeker must pass beyond them; they are not a final goal.
rows.anchor: نعم يظهر في أثناء الطريق علوم ومعارف كثيرة ولكن لا بد من العبور عنها

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: Sirhindī says law and spiritual reality are one in truth, differing by summary versus detail, inference versus unveiling, and effort versus ease; any contradiction, however slight, proves nonattainment.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن الشريعة والحقيقة متحدان في الحقيقة ولا فرق بينهما إلا بالإجمال والتفصيل

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: Sirhindī says the phrase that law is a shell and reality its kernel may be defensible only as summary compared with detail, though the wording misleads.
rows.anchor: وما وقع في عبارة بعض المشايخ من أن الشريعة قشر والحقيقة لب

rows.speaker: عبد القادر الكيلاني
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Jīlānī says saints draw only on God's and the Messenger's words and act only by their outward meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال سيدي القطب الرباني الشيخ عبد القادر الكيلاني قدس سره : جميع الأولياء

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd says every path is closed except following the Messenger; he also says this discipline is bound by Quran and Sunna and its teacher must know both.
rows.anchor: وقال سيد الطائفة الجنيد قدس سره : الطرق كلها مسدودة إلا على من اقتفى أثر الرسول

rows.speaker: السري السقطي
rows.claim: Al-Sarī al-Saqaṭī says spiritual insight must preserve scrupulousness, never contradict scripture, and never use miracles as a pretext to violate God's prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وقال السري السقطي : التصوف اسم لثلاثة معان وهو لا يطفيء نور معرفته نور ورعه

rows.speaker: أبو الحسين النوري
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Nūrī says to avoid anyone claiming a spiritual state beyond religious learning and to distrust claims unsupported by outward law.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين النوري : من رأيته يدعي مع الله تعالى حالة تخرجه عن جد العلم الشرعي

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz says every inward inspiration contradicted by outward teaching is false.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخراز : كل فيض باطن يخالفه ظاهر فهو باطل

rows.speaker: أبو العباس أحمد الدينوري
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad al-Dīnawarī says inward reality does not change the ruling of outward law.
rows.anchor: وقالأبو العباس أحمد الدينوري : لسان الظاهر لا يغير حكم الباطن

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī says one who claims a spiritual state exempts him from prayer or permits wine should be killed; the author says there is no doubt about eternal punishment because this is apostasy.
rows.anchor: وفي التحفة لابن حجر قال الغزالي : من زعم أن له مع الله تعالى حالا

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī says anyone claiming inner truth can contradict outward law is closer to unbelief than faith.
rows.anchor: وقال في الإحياء : من قال إن الباطل يخالف الظاهر فهو إلى الكفر أقرب منه إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says mystics do receive unseen disclosures, but these are fruits of sincerity within religious law and cannot change legal rulings, restrict an unrestricted ruling, or release a restricted one.
rows.anchor: فإن الكشوف والعلوم الغيبية ثمرة الإخلاص الذي هو الجزء الثالث من أجزاء الشريعة

rows.speaker: ساجقلي زاده
rows.claim: Sājūqlīzāda says hidden causes may make Khidr's ship damage and killing lawful exceptions to general prohibitions; the author says earlier texts explicitly reject this.
rows.anchor: خلافا لما توهمه ساجقلي زاده حيث قال في شرح عبارة الإحياء السابقة آنفا

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: Sirhindī says mystical unveilings and experiences are not final goals; they train beginners, and the accomplished seeker passes beyond them toward contentment, a rare attainment.
rows.anchor: أنها تربي بها أطفال الطريق وأنه ينبغي مجاوزتها والوصول إلى مقام الرضا

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: Those who mistake ecstatic states and visions for spiritual goals remain trapped in illusion and miss the law's full attainments.
rows.anchor: إن الذين هم قليلو النظر يعدون الأحوال والمواجيد من المقامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is more complete than Khidr; Khidr's greater knowledge of inner reality was relative to their present states, while Moses passed beyond it in his lawgiving role.
rows.anchor: ويعلم مما ذكر أن موسى عليه السلام أكمل من الخضر وأعلمية الخضر عليه السلام بعلم الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Mathnawī verse illustrates that a lover's passion can eclipse the formal lessons of Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī; the author says a perfected person may even be hidden among ordinary people.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يخرج بيت المثنوي حيث يقول : زان طرف كه عشق من افزوددرد بو حنيفة شافعي درسي نكرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story has Ḥabīb al-ʿAjamī find al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī waiting for a boat; Ḥabīb asks whether al-Ḥasan lacks certainty, and al-Ḥasan asks whether he lacks knowledge.
rows.anchor: إن الحسن البصري وقف على شط نهر ينتظر سفينة فجاء حبيب العجمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan is superior in the story because he combines knowledge and direct vision, seeing that divine power operates through wise natural causes; Ḥabīb's ecstatic state overlooks those causes.
rows.anchor: أن الفضل للحسن فإنه كان جامعا بين علم اليقين وعين اليقين

rows.speaker: أحمد السرهندي
rows.claim: Sirhindī compares the end of Uways, the master of the Successors, with the beginning of Waḥshī, Ḥamza's killer, after conversion, to explain the rarity of miracles among Companions.
rows.anchor: مع قول الإمام الرباني : إن نهاية أويس سيد التابعين بداية وحشي قاتل حمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest perfected person is the Prophet, who continually rises through descent and descends through ascent; he is the fullest union of spiritual reality and revealed law.
rows.anchor: وليس ذلك إلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولولا ذلك ما أمد العالم

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī divides afterlife knowledge into unveiling and practice; unveiling is a light in a purified heart clarifying knowledge of God, His attributes, acts, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: أما علم المكاشفة فهو علم الباطن وهو غاية العلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Bulqīnī's claim that unveiling conflicts with outward knowledge, since prophets rank above the truthful and the two forms coexist; he cites the hierarchy in 4:69.
rows.anchor: ولعمري لقد أخطأ فيما قال وبالحق تعرف الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story cannot establish that inner knowledge conflicts with law. The boy's killing was a special rule for Khidr; if he was a saint rather than prophet, another prophet may have conveyed the command.
rows.anchor: إن قصة الخضر عليه السلام لا تصلح حجة لمن يزعم المخالفة بين العلمين

rows.speaker: السبكي
rows.claim: Al-Subkī says Khidr received revelation to act according to inward reality in this exceptional case; Islamic law never permits killing a child, especially one born to believing parents, for a future offense.
rows.anchor: أوحي إليه أن يعمل بالباطن وخلاف الظاهر الموافق للحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising the wall without wages is unobjectionable kindness, even if the beneficiaries were wrongdoers, and reflects noble character.
rows.anchor: وأما إقامة الجدار بلا أجر فلا إشكال فيها لأنها إحسان

rows.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Al-ʿIzz b. ʿAbd al-Salām says a guardian must damage a ward's property when necessary to keep an oppressor from taking it; the guardian's claim of preserving it is accepted later.
rows.anchor: يجب عليه تعييبه لأجل حفظه وكان القول قول من عيب مال اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a corrupt judge would seize a ward's property unless paid, the guardian must offer the smallest amount that prevents its loss; the guardian's account is accepted later.
rows.anchor: فإنه يجب عليه أن يدفع إليه شيئا ويتحرى في أقل ما يمكن إرضاؤه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative supports traveling for knowledge, honoring teachers, avoiding premature objections, interpreting puzzling conduct charitably, keeping promises, apologizing, and a teacher explaining why a student cannot yet be taught.
rows.anchor: من استحباب الرحلة للعلم وفضل طلبه واستحباب استعمال الأدب مع العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It permits taking a servant and provisions on a journey without compromising trust in God; forgetfulness may be attributed figuratively to Satan out of reverence and is not blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وعلى جواز اتخاذ الخادم في السفر وحمل الزاد فيه وأنه لا ينافي التوكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story supports stating intentions with God's will, setting conditions between leader and follower, and treating three as a meaningful count in repetition.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المشيئة في الأمر واشتراط المتبوع على التابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It supports riding boats, judging by outward appearances until contrary evidence appears, doing good even to scoundrels, taking payment for work, and burying property for safekeeping.
rows.anchor: وعلى جواز ركوب السفينة وفيه الحكم بالظاهر حتى يتبين خلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Owning an earning tool or insufficient property does not end poverty; usurpation is forbidden, and the story indicates saintly miracles if Khidr was a wali.
rows.anchor: وأن المسكين لا يخرج عن المسكنة بملك آلة يكتسب بها

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارة
rows.claim: Mystical interpreters read God's servant as a special intimate detached from others; the highest distinction is being related to God's comprehensive name or pronoun, reserved here for Muhammad.
rows.anchor: على ما ذكره بعض أهل الإشارة ( فوجدا عبدا من عبادنا ) فيه إشارة

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارة
rows.claim: They interpret mercy from God as nearness to Him and knowledge taught from Him as special knowledge received directly from God.
rows.anchor: وهي مرتبة القرب منه عز وجل ( وعلمناه من لدنا علما ) وهو العلم الخاص

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Dhū al-Nūn defines divinely bestowed knowledge as knowledge that governs creatures through the points of success and abandonment.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو النون : العلم اللدني هو الذي يحكم على الخلق بمواقع التوفيق والخذلان

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd describes it as direct disclosure of secrets and hidden matters, attained by guarding the limbs from disobedience and emptying one's actions of personal desire.
rows.anchor: وقال الجنيد قدس سره : هو الإطلاع على الأسرار من غير ظن فيه

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارة
rows.claim: Other definitions describe it as knowledge of what benefits God's servants, unseen knowledge of acts, insight into predestination before events occur, knowledge of divine names and attributes, or knowledge of the divine essence.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو علم يعرف به الحق سبحانه أولياءه ما فيه صلاح عباده
